one_line_reason: The strongest single-ingredient human evidence (Cochrane review of hawthorn monopreparations) is exclusively in diagnosed chronic heart failure patients, a clinical population and a cardiac medical claim, not general supplement use.

selected.population: patients with chronic heart failure, NYHA stage II (per German Commission E indication cited)
selected.intervention: hawthorn leaf-and-flower extract monopreparations, oral, double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (abstract as retrieved is truncated before dose/result details)
selected.primary_outcome: benefits and harms of hawthorn extract in chronic heart failure (symptom/exercise-tolerance measures implied by review scope)
selected.why_selected: The definitive single-ingredient Cochrane systematic review of hawthorn monopreparation RCTs; the retrieved abstract text is cut off before stating pooled results, so direction cannot be read from what is available

selected.intervention: fixed combination of hawthorn extract and camphor (Korodin Herz-Kreislauf-Tropfen®), oral, RCTs pooled (4 trials, 221 patients)
selected.primary_outcome: systolic and diastolic blood pressure, cognition
selected.why_selected: Only shortlisted RCT meta-analysis with a clearly stated directional result (BP increase), included despite being a 2-ingredient combination product rather than hawthorn alone

blockers: 18254076's population is diagnosed chronic heart failure (NYHA II) patients under medical supervision, a clinical claim area rather than general wellness use

31255877 studies a fixed 2-ingredient branded combination product (hawthorn + camphor, Korodin®), not hawthorn alone, and the outcome (raising blood pressure in hypotension) is a different use case from the cardiovascular-support claims typical of catalog hawthorn products

Several other shortlisted reviews (42277690, 38706368, 37644446, 22718512, 23975682) evaluate hawthorn only as one ingredient among many plant extracts or multi-herb TCM formulations, so no hawthorn-specific effect size can be attributed from those abstracts

handoff_pmids.note: Systematic review of the adverse-event profile of Crataegus (hawthorn) monopreparations, including drug-interaction data collected from manufacturers and spontaneous reporting

excluded_pmids.reason: Network meta-analysis of 15 different plant extracts (including hawthorn) for heart failure; abstract does not state hawthorn's individual ranking/effect separate from the other 14 extracts
Systematic review of multi-herb TCM combination regimens for MASLD; hawthorn is not evaluated as a standalone exposure
General review of herbal interventions for cardiovascular disease covering many herbs (Moringa, ginseng, Ginkgo, etc.); no hawthorn-specific data given
Review of multiple medicinal/food-homologous substances for NAFLD; not hawthorn-specific
Meta-analysis of combined Western medicine plus traditional Chinese medicine (acupuncture and herbs) for stroke rehabilitation; not specific to hawthorn
Broad review of nutraceuticals in heart failure (PUFA, CoQ10, iron); hawthorn is not identifiable as a focus of the retrieved abstract text
Cochrane review of herbal medicines for fatty liver disease; Crataegus pinnatifida is one of several herbs discussed, not isolated
Systematic review of TCM formulations for NAFLD; hawthorn appears only as one of 246 herbs used across 419 multi-herb formulations
Study of custodial vs non-custodial criminal sanctions; 'Hawthorn effects' refers to the Hawthorne observer-effect concept, unrelated to the herb
